newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at new record, dollar strong.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at new record, dollar strong.

text.p: Dutch shares closed almost two percent higher and near the days' peak as a firmer dollar boosted market sentiment.
Dealers said money was still flowing into the market and they did not see an end of the upswing in the near-term, although Wall Street started to fall after a higher opening.
"Private investors are still very keen to invest money into the market, especially in high tech stocks," said one dealer.
The AEX share index closed 17.33 points higher at 935.37 and touched an all-time high of 936.65 earlier today.
The AMX midcap index rose 20.05 points to 1401.92.
Financials were in demand all day with investors still keen on buying financial services group ING after yesterday's U.S. acquisition news.
ING added 3.50 guilders to 105.40, after briefly touching 106.60. On Tuesday the stock rose 6.30 guilders.
Other financials were also strong as result of a firmer bond market. The gains in the bond market faded after the Dutch share market had closed.
ABN AMRO bank added 1.90 guilders or 4.6 percent to a new high of 43.30 guilders.
Software firm Cap Gemini rose strongly after it announced a 30 percent increase in first half results late on Tuesday and analysts said they were very upbeat on the stock.
Cap Gemini closed 5.30 guilders higher at 71.10, after touching a year-high of 71.60 earlier.
Dealers said volumes were high in Cap Gemini.
Publisher Wolters Kluwer gained 12.00 guilders to 260.90 after investment bank Goldman Sachs rated the stock as a market outperformer.
Shares in paper maker KNP BT shed most of the day's gains near the close at 43.60, up 0.90 on Tuesdays close.

Dealers said KNP BT rose strongly in early trade following the news that U.S. International Paper would restructure its business, an announcement which had a positive impact on the share price of the U.S. firm last night.
"It looked as if the real recovery for KNP BT started, but most of the gains had faded near the close of the Dutch share market and the direction is not clear," said one dealer.
Electronics firm Philips also touched a new high at 148.20 and closed 4.50 guilders up at 147.80.
